subject: Observability data custody & SIEM mapping — on-prem handoff
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tom Berg <tom.berg@medsys.io>, security@acmehealth.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability data custody & SIEM mapping — on-prem handoff

Hi Tom / MedSys security team,

Per our onboarding checklist, we'd like to lock down the observability handoff for your private deployment (on-prem cluster in your Azure stack). Goal is to confirm: SIEM ingestion endpoints, what data stays in your tenancy vs exported to Redwood for transient processing, and the exact field-level mapping the SOC expects.

Attached is our current data-path diagram and the internal evidence checklist (redwood-obsv-data-map-v1.pdf, evidence-checklist.xlsx). Can you review and confirm the following by EOD Wednesday so we can schedule the runbook walk-through?

- Is Splunk HEC (HTTPS) or syslog over mTLS your preferred ingestion path?
- Token / certificate rotation cadence you require and where tokens are stored (KMS / Vault)?
- Retention policy for debug traces vs metrics vs syslogs in your SIEM (days)
- Any PII redaction rules we need to apply before shipping (we can apply prefix scrubbing or redact at the forwarder)

We also want to validate trace-span tagging expectations so our tracing hook doesn't drop important attributes. Kimberly, Marissa — looping you in to add technical constraints.

Thanks — happy to run a short call after you confirm the ingestion path.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-obsv-data-map-v1.pdf (diagram), evidence-checklist.xlsx (checklist)

From: Tom Berg <tom.berg@medsys.io>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, support@medsys-ops.com
Date: Mon, 27 May 2029 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Observability data custody & SIEM mapping — on-prem handoff

Laura — thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers up front, then a couple of clarifying Qs.

- Preferred ingestion: Splunk HEC (HTTPS) for structured events; syslog over TLS for legacy appliances. HEC is preferred where possible.
- Token rotation: quarterly. We use an internal Vault (HashiCorp) for secrets; HEC tokens are stored there with ACLs.
- Retention: logs 365 days, metrics 90 days, traces 30 days. Can we request traces be sampled at 1:100 for production?
- PII: our compliance team requires removing full SSNs and PII-like identifiers from log payloads before they leave our VLAN. Masking on the forwarder is fine.

I've attached our SIEM onboarding template (medsys-siem-template.docx) and an internal field map we use. A couple of clarifying items:

1) Do you expect Redwood to persist any observability artifacts in your environment, or will everything be forwarded live to our SIEM?
2) For tracing hooks: can you accept OpenTelemetry semantic conventions; we will provide a sample span with the tag set we expect.

If it's helpful, I can set up a quick tech check at 14:00 ET today.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2029 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability data custody & SIEM mapping — on-prem handoff

Tom / MedSys — thanks for the quick reply and the attachments. A few technical notes from our side to make the deployment smooth:

- Ingestion & auth:
  * We support Splunk HEC over HTTPS (preferred) and syslog/tls. HEC tokens are configurable per-forwarder; we recommend storing them in Vault and mounting to the forwarder via a K8s secret projection (or using the on-prem agent's built-in Vault integration).
  * We also support mTLS for syslog; cert rotation scripts can be included in the runbook.

- Data residency model:
  * Redwood Private will not persist raw logs in our cloud. By default we ship events from the forwarder directly to your SIEM; we may temporarily cache small batches for retry (up to 2 hours) but we can configure zero-persistence mode if required.

- Tracing hooks / spans:
  * We emit OpenTelemetry spans by default. We'll add a small config to keep the following attributes at sample-time: request_id, customer_id (hashed), span.kind, model_id, prompt_length. If you need additional PII redaction, we can add a transform before export.

- Field mapping: attached is a CSV mapping we use internally for Splunk sourcetypes and field names. Please confirm the sourcetype you want us to use for inference-events (default: redwood:inference:event).

Next steps:
- Laura: propose runbook times
- Tom / Security: confirm preferred sourcetype + any redaction rules
- We'll prepare an evidence packet aligned with your SOC checklist before the runbook (evidence-checklist.xlsx)

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Infra Engineer, Private Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Observability data custody & SIEM mapping — on-prem handoff

Tom — this is perfect, thanks. Quick confirmations and plan:

- We will default to Splunk HEC for inference-events and syslog/tls as fallback for legacy appliances.
- We'll implement a zero-persistence policy for raw logs (only short-lived retry cache configurable) and document that in the runbook.
- Traces: agree to 1:100 sampling for production; we will emit OpenTelemetry spans and include the attribute set Kimberly listed.
- PII: Redwood will apply configurable scrubbing transforms at the forwarder; please send any specific regexes or fields you require redacted by EOD tomorrow.

Planned next steps:
- Tech check: 14:00 ET today (Tom please confirm)
- Runbook draft sent to MedSys by Wed EOD (we'll attach an evidence bundle aligned with your SOC review)
- Post-runbook: 2-week P0 monitoring window and a handoff sign-off once evidence items are validated

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the tech check.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced earlier: redwood-obsv-data-map-v1.pdf, evidence-checklist.xlsx
